title: GPU softlock + traceback incident notes and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

Short version: a subset of GPUs in cluster-a intermittently entered a softlocked state during high-concurrency inference bursts (2029-08-14 23:12->23:40 UTC). Symptoms: long-running kernel (hang), periodic kernel tracebacks visible in dmesg (gpu_crashed, ttm_lockup), and recoveries only after node reboot. Not an immediate fleet-wide outage but correlated with a rise in correctable ECC counts and transient nvlink negotiation errors.

Why this doc exists:
- capture oncall observations and log excerpts before they disappear
- draft a minimal operational checklist to reduce MTTR next time
- list hypotheses and experiments to prioritize for follow-up (SRE + Serving)

Observations (raw):
- Alerts: repeated "gpu-hung-kernel" alerts (p95 45s to 120s) during the window.
- Telemetry: per-GPU ECC correctable counter spikes on GPUs 3/4/7 within node-237; NVLink errors (negotiation timeout) logged on peer ports around same timestamps.
- dmesg excerpts (redacted):
  [Aug 14 23:18:03] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=54321: Graphics Exception: ESR 0x3b
  [Aug 14 23:18:04] gpu_sched: runaway kernel detected on GPU 3, killing
  [Aug 14 23:18:05] nvlink: lane 1 negotiated timeout on link 0
  [Aug 14 23:19:10] kernel: watchdog: gpu hung - attempt reset failed

- User workload: 3 concurrent model-serving pods pinned to node-237 (dedicated GPU assignment). Burst pattern: many short chat requests, many small sequences (~50 tokens). Batching disabled on these routes.

Immediate mitigations tried (what we did oncall):
- Offlined node-237 from scheduler (k8s cordon + drain) to stop incoming work (T+10m).
- Attempted soft-reset via nvidia-smi --gpu-reset on GPU 3 (failed with "Not supported on this device").
- Tried driver hot-unload (modprobe -r nvidia) — blocked by active contexts.
- Rebooted the host (T+24m) — node returned healthy, workloads rescheduled.
- Rolled a temporary routing rule to avoid that rack for the last-hour burst (manual RB policy).

What didn't fit initial assumptions:
- Not a single-driver version regression: node had driver v540.82, same as many other stable nodes.
- Not simple thermal: sensors showed normal temps (peak 72C). PSU logs clean.
- ECC correctable surges were local to a small set of GPUs, not global.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVLink negotiation instability + transient ECC bursts cause the scheduler/driver to encounter a long-running recovery path, leading to softlocks.
2) A specific model kernel path with many short dispatches exposes a driver race under heavy context-switch churn (workload-specific).
3) Intermittent PCIe parity glitches causing the driver to spin during recovery.
4) Rare firmware/retimer edgecase where NVLink link training fails and the driver enters blocking retry loop.

Quick tests to run (postmortem sprint):
- Reproduce workload in lab with identical driver/firmware and synthetic bursts (use stress script below).
- Toggle NVLink (where supported) to test without peer links (isolation test).
- Run driver with debug logging (NVRM_LOG_LEVEL=7) and capture full dmesg during replay.
- Run a kernel microbenchmark that dispatches many tiny kernels to simulate high context churn.

Temporary runbook draft (minimal for oncall):
1) If you see repeated "gpu-hung-kernel" and dmesg shows nvlink negotiation errors:
   - Cordon the node and drain pods (kubectl cordon; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data).
   - Increase oncall alert severity and notify serving-team pager.
2) Try a per-GPU reset (nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <id>). If unsupported/fails, proceed to host reboot.
3) If reboot succeeded and node returns healthy, leave node cordoned for 30m and ramp traffic slowly via routing rule.
4) If node reboots but exhibits immediate recurrence, capture full memory (dmesg + nvtop + nvidia-smi -q -d ALL) and escalate to infra-release (possible firmware/driver rollback candidate).

Checklist for capture (one-liners to run during incident):
- dmesg --level=err,warn | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-err.txt
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -l 1 --loop=10 > /tmp/nvsmi-sample.csv
- cat /sys/class/powercap/*/constraints/* (verify power capping)
- nvlink status: for each peer run nvidia-smi nvlink --status (if supported)
- extract backtrace from kernel logs: journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -i 'gpu' -A5 -B5 > /tmp/gpu-backtrace.txt

Follow-ups & experiments (owners):
- SRE/Serving: run replay harness against lab with low-latency chat workload and measure ECC counts and nvlink logs. (Owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Infra: schedule firmware/retimer validation against node image; identify nodes with specific retimer versions. (Owner: Diego Ruiz)
- Runtime team: add a lightweight watchdog that records pre-reset GPU context snapshot to help identify stuck kernel types. (Owner: Hannah Park)

Longer-term mitigations to consider:
- Add automatic fallback routing when a node shows repeated nvlink/ECC spikes (automated quarantine for 10m).
- Instrument per-kernel dispatch timing in runtime to detect workloads that produce extreme small-kernel churn.
- Improve alerting: require combined signal (gpu-hung + nvlink errors OR ECC burst) before auto-escalation to reduce noise.
- Work with driver vendor on edge-case retry loops observed in kernel tracebacks; provide logs and dmesg for repro.

Questions to resolve (open):
- Are the offending GPUs all from the same hardware batch/lot? (serial numbers captured)
- Any correlation with rack-level PDUs or network fabric events at those timestamps? (PDUs show no obvious blips)
- Why did nvidia-smi --gpu-reset report "not supported" on a board that previously accepted reset? (possible firmware change)

Ephemeral test script (quick synthetic workload):
- loop.sh (run on a lab node with two GPUs pinned)
  for i in {1..2000}; do
    # launch tiny kernel via cudacall smallvector (custom harness)
    ./tiny_infer --device 0 --seq-length 48 --batch 1 &
    ./tiny_infer --device 1 --seq-length 48 --batch 1 &
    wait
    sleep 0.05
  done

- capture ECC counters in parallel (see checklist).

Notes to self / handoff to Monday (Hannah/Liam):
- Attach the full dmesg and nvidia-smi captures to JIRA INFRA-12987.
- Re-run fleet-health query to list nodes with similar ECC spike patterns in last 30 days.
- If we can repro in lab, try downgrading to driver v535.x as a bisect axis.

Appendix: quick log timeline (condensed)
- 2029-08-14 23:12 UTC — first gpu-hung alert for node-237
- 2029-08-14 23:15 UTC — second alert; ECC correctable counters rising on GPU 3
- 2029-08-14 23:18 UTC — dmesg shows nvlink negotiation timeout and gfx ESR errors
- 2029-08-14 23:22 UTC — tried per-gpu reset (failed)
- 2029-08-14 23:36 UTC — host rebooted, node returns
- 2029-08-14 23:40 UTC — traffic routed away from rack temporarily

TODO:
- [ ] Upload full artifacts to JIRA & Confluence (Maya)
- [ ] Add short A/B test for routing fallback automation (SRE)
- [ ] Run lab repro (Serving + SRE) and capture debug-driver logs

End of notes.

(Informal tone retained; we'll convert to a more formal postmortem if repro steps confirm a root cause.)
